content.title: About
content.content: Barley bread is made from whole barley grain or flour, often blended with wheat. It has a dense crumb, a mildly nutty flavor, and a dark‑golden crust. Barley is rich in fiber and β‑glucan, making this bread nutritious and filling.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Barley is one of the oldest cultivated grains, grown by humans for over 10,000 years.
In ancient Egypt barley bread was offered to the gods as a sacred food.
The high β‑glucan content can help lower cholesterol levels.
Barley contains antioxidants such as selenium and vitamin E.
Traditional Scandinavian “rugbrød” often combines barley and rye flours.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestion, promotes satiety, and helps regulate blood sugar.

items.title: Contains β‑glucan
items.content: This soluble fiber can reduce LDL cholesterol and support immune function.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Barley provides thiamine, niacin, and folate, essential for energy metabolism.

items.title: Rich in minerals
items.content: It supplies magnesium, phosphorus, iron, and zinc, which aid muscle and nerve health.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Compared with white wheat bread, barley bread raises blood glucose more slowly.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Barley contains gluten, so the product is unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High phytic acid
items.content: Phytic acid can impair mineral absorption; soaking or fermenting the dough can reduce its level.

items.title: Cereal allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to barley.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Barley bread works well toasted, in sandwiches, as a soup side, or as a base for breadcrumbs. It can be grilled with olive oil and herbs or used for open‑face toppings.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the bread in a paper bag or bread box at room temperature for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze it in an airtight bag for up to 2 months. Thaw at room temperature before use.
